clue.text: Act less, try broadcast for radio once

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of these words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre director tells an overacting performer to tone it down on an old wireless show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the radio picture, but it signals that ACT LESS TRY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An early wireless receiver using a mineral detector was the kind of radio people built at home long ago.

clue.text: Girl including work on piano for ballet

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the other pieces into its middle, holding them within

parts.note: Celia is a girl's name
OP is short for opus, a work
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A young dancer practises a piece on the piano for her ballet class.
explanation.definitionFit: Delibes's comic ballet about a lifelike doll is a classic of the dance repertoire.

clue.text: See 15
Main areas for catch, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that a word's spoken form stands in for one spelt differently

parts.note: to catch something is to seize it

explanation.surface: A fisherman talks about the big waters where the catch is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the old poetic word for the ocean, so 'Main areas' are oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the open ocean, and its areas are the great bodies of salt water.

clue.text: Is a bit less liable to change

definitions.text: Is a bit less liable to change

indicators.note: letters liable to change may be shifted around, signalling a rearrangement of the words before them

explanation.surface: Something that steadies itself becomes slightly less volatile.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and IS A BIT LESS, rearranged as 'liable to change' signals, spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that steadies becomes firmer and so is less prone to alteration.

clue.text: Offhand opponent of parliamentarian

definitions.meaning: offhand means casually dismissive or high-handed
in the English Civil War the Royalists fought the Roundheads, who backed Parliament

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark from a political rival.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1640s English Civil War, a Royalist soldier was known by this name and fought the Parliamentarians.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both careless or dismissive and a Royalist supporter of Charles I in the Civil War.

clue.text: Parties around Asian school a lot

indicators.note: the word for parties sits around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: dos are parties, as in a big do
Zen is a school of Buddhism from East Asia

explanation.surface: Lots of parties take place around a school in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of twelve used loosely mean a great many, as in 'dozens of times'.

clue.text: Dates, mostly 19, in Rome — that is to say, short

indicators.note: short means the phrase is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: id est, abbreviated i.e., is Latin for that is to say

explanation.surface: A note on Roman calendar days, explained briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is THIRTEEN: in the Roman calendar these days fell on the 13th in most months, the 15th in four. ID EST loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar these were the mid-month days, usually the thirteenth.

clue.text: President and first lady left in resting place

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed inside the word for a resting place

parts.note: a roost is where birds rest
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A US president and his First Lady leave their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Two US presidents, Theodore and Franklin D., carried this surname.

clue.text: Admitted audibly, not silently

indicators.note: audibly tells us to take the spoken form of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: admitted means allowed in

explanation.surface: Someone confesses something out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in an audible voice is the opposite of keeping quiet.

clue.text: Soldier in areas of shooting, such as 4 and 22 across

indicators.note: the soldier's abbreviation goes inside the word for filming locations

parts.note: film sets are the areas where scenes are shot
Pte is the abbreviation for private, a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier stationed in areas where gunfire is common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it is filming. 4 and 22 across complete the Seven Seas and Seven Samurai, groups of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of seven, such as the seven oceans or the seven Japanese warriors of the film.

clue.text: A king dividing drinks in glass containers

indicators.note: dividing means the pieces split the word for drinks by going into it

parts.note: beers are drinks
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch shares out drinks in glass vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory vessels of glass with a lip for pouring.

clue.text: Great weightlifter's world record?

definitions.meaning: the Titan of Greek myth condemned to hold up the heavens
a book of maps is a record of the world

explanation.surface: A champion lifter sets a new world best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world record' looks like a sporting feat; it is a book of maps, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan who bore the sky and the book of maps of the world share the name.

clue.text: Perversely cite case about line that's between Ireland and part of UK

definitions.text: between Ireland and part of UK

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the abbreviation, enclosing it
perversely means in a wayward manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly quotes a legal case about a boundary line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the letters of CITE CASE, jumbled as 'Perversely' signals, around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of sea south of Ireland and west of Wales and Cornwall bears this name.

clue.text: Warm, holding temperature? That's natural

indicators.note: the word for warm holds the abbreviation within it

parts.note: congenial means warm and friendly

explanation.surface: A medical note queries a fever, then concludes it is a natural state.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition present from birth is innate, so natural to the person.

clue.text: Attending 19 when divided in confusion

parts.note: at means attending, as at a meeting
19-across gives thirteen, which split into two parts is six and seven

explanation.surface: Someone attends a meeting that splits apart in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 refers to the answer at 19 across, thirteen; divided, thirteen becomes six and seven, as plurals.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a state of disorder or muddle.

clue.text: Standard combination of top players and bands, originally 19

parts.note: stars are the top players in a team or cast
stripes are bands of colour

explanation.surface: A flag made of elite players and coloured bands, first with thirteen of each.
explanation.walkthrough: A standard is a flag here. 'originally 19' adds that the first US flag had thirteen of each, thirteen being 19 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the national flag of the United States.

clue.text: A statue damaged crossing river in flood

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go across the abbreviation, holding it inside
damaged means the letters are knocked out of shape, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A statue is damaged as a river bursts its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts the letters of A STATUE, rearranged as 'damaged' signals, around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something thoroughly is to drench it, as a flood does.

clue.text: President strangely agin dancing

parts.note: James Polk was the eleventh US president

indicators.note: strangely means the letters behave oddly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A president, oddly, is against dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agin' is dialect for against, but here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing the lively Bohemian dance in two-four time.

clue.text: 7 for 12 without second — isn't there, somehow

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters are arranged by some unspecified means into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled note about a number that isn't present.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is DOZENS, 12 is BEAKERS; without its second letter that is BAKERS. A baker's dozen is thirteen, and the definition reads as 'baker's dozens'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker's dozen is an old term for a set of one more than twelve.

clue.text: The writer's on vehicle, producing a bit of poetry

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I; the writer's is I am
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An author reports from a vehicle, producing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one weak then one strong syllable is a small unit of verse.

clue.text: Assembles in large groups, we hear, in plant

indicators.note: we hear tells us a word is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: people flock when they gather in crowds

explanation.surface: Crowds gather around a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower grown for its clusters of bright blooms.

clue.text: Prepares three and nineteen, or one of 3 and one of 19, for example

definitions.meaning: to prepare a surface or a pump is to get it ready for action

definitions.text: three and nineteen, or one of 3 and one of 19, for example
definitions.meaning: three and nineteen, and seven and thirteen from 3 and 19, are all numbers divisible only by one and themselves

explanation.surface: A list of numbers, each prepared in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is SEVENS and 19 across is THIRTEENS, so 'one of 3' is seven and 'one of 19' is thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting ready is priming; numbers with no factors but one and themselves are this kind of number.

clue.text: Warriors putting spirit back into Asia, perhaps

indicators.note: the turned piece goes into the rearranged letters
perhaps means the word given is one possible arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled
back means the word for spirit is turned round

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Fighters bringing spirit back to Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes SAAI and 'back' gives MUR, which 'into' places inside; 'Asia, perhaps' reads like an example of a continent, but it is a shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Inauspicious number of clubs, for example, in match

definitions.text: Inauspicious number of clubs, for example
definitions.meaning: thirteen cards of clubs make up one complete set in a pack
to match is to go well with, to be fitting

explanation.surface: An unlucky count of golf clubs used in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirteen is the unlucky number; a full set of clubs in a pack of cards is thirteen. 'clubs' suggests golf.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four sets of thirteen cards in a pack, and also a verb meaning to fit or befit.

clue.text: On particular dates, supposedly dangerous times I had in battles

definitions.text: On particular dates, supposedly dangerous times

indicators.note: the contraction goes inside the word for battles

parts.note: frays are fights or battles
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: On certain days, superstitious people find danger in battles.
explanation.walkthrough: The dates are the 13th; the weekday falling then is supposedly unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth weekday is thought unlucky when it falls on the thirteenth of a month.

clue.text: Reaction of some to 19, loudly hearing organ

parts.note: F is the musical abbreviation for forte, loudly
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Some people react to hearing a loud number.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is THIRTEEN; dread of thirteen is triskaidekaphobia.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstitious dread is how some people respond to the number thirteen.

clue.text: North Americans elected that object about university

parts.note: a party elected to office is in
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: Elected officials argue about a university project.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous peoples of Arctic Canada, Alaska and Greenland.

clue.text: A brave military leader — not for Paris

definitions.text: A brave military leader — not for Paris

parts.note: game means brave or willing

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: non is French for not, as spoken in Paris

explanation.surface: A courageous general who will not side with Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines him: the Greek commander against Troy, the side of Paris, abductor of Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king led the army that besieged Troy, the city of Paris.
